designs.title: Summit Ridge
designs.why: Separates cleanly (no sub-0.5 mm strokes, no specks), but the hatching is wormy threshold texture rather than drawn strokes, the 6,861 m summit is a small weak peak, and a dead band of shirt splits the two ranges so it reads as two prints from 3 m. The five climbers are too small to be seen.
designs.fix: Redraw the rock shading as continuous directional strokes and close the gap between the ranges so the summit and the roped team make one tall, connected image.

designs.title: Kitesurfing
designs.why: Bold solids and clean line make a strong one-hit print on the black main tee. The long kite lines hold at about 0.5 mm, and there are no plugging areas apart from the harness detail. The letterspaced KITESURFING word is thin and tiny next to the figure.
designs.fix: Make the wordmark heavier and about 1.5x larger so it holds on black and balances the figure.

designs.title: Coral
designs.why: A handsome plate with good coverage (13%) and clean edges. The bubbly shadow texture in the trunk carries clusters of pinhole openings that will fill in on a 156 mesh and turn to mottled solid, and the CORAL. caption is undersized.
designs.fix: Open the trunk shadow texture so the gaps are at least 0.3 mm (or commit those areas to solid) and enlarge the caption.

designs.title: Antarctica
designs.why: A clear silhouette group with a strong heading, and it reads at distance. The penguin backs are a mesh of 1-3 px openings (about 1,900 holes) that will fill in to muddy, uneven blacks, and the lineup is stiff and symmetrical.
designs.fix: Make the dark plumage either clean solid or hatching with at least 0.3 mm openings, so the backs print as an intended black rather than gained-up mud.

designs.title: Bait Ball
designs.why: The strongest graphic idea here: the spiral reads instantly from 3 m and suits one ink on black. The core is about 70% ink, so fish merge there and will gain into a blotch, while the outermost fish are tiny.
designs.fix: Thin the fish in the centre of the spiral with clear negative space between bodies so the core stays readable after dot gain.

designs.title: Beluga
designs.why: Only 5% coverage: a big empty outline with stipple clumps full of 1 px pinholes (about 4,400) that will print as solid blobs. On black the body is just a thin contour, so it reads weak for a $50 shirt, and the bold caption looks blobby.
designs.fix: Model the body with an even stipple or line gradient across its whole form (dots at least 0.35 mm), so the whale has volume and the print has presence.

designs.title: Humpback Whale
designs.why: A well-organised plate with good engraving and clean separation. The labels are about 2 mm cap height and cannot be read beyond arm's length, and mechanical checker-dot tone patches sit inside hand-drawn hatching and will fill in or mottle.
designs.fix: Raise the label type to at least 3 mm cap height (or cut half the labels), and replace the checker-dot tone with line hatching.

designs.title: Octopus
designs.why: The best print in the set: a strong silhouette, good 16% coverage, rhythmic suckers and clean edges that will print crisp. The only flaw is a mechanical checker-tone patch around the eye and mantle, with 4 px openings that will partly fill in and looks out of place in hand engraving.
designs.fix: Replace the checker tone at the eye and mantle with hand stipple or hatching with openings of at least 0.35 mm.

designs.title: Patagonia
designs.why: The open line prints clean with no plugging, but at 6.5% coverage it is faint from 3 m on the black main tee. The peak labels are small and rough-edged like traced bitmap type (Fitz Roy shows a blobby fi and commas). San Lorenzo (3,706 m) is labelled higher than Fitz Roy but drawn lower.
designs.fix: Reset all labels and the caption as clean vector type at 3 mm or larger, and add weight and shading to the foreground and main peaks so the panorama carries at distance.

designs.title: El Calafate
designs.why: Crisp, legible type and very clean separation (few small openings), so it is the easiest print here. The El Calafate 0 km arm anchors it well. It is narrow (7.4 in) and type-heavy, so it reads as a souvenir sign more than a drawing.
designs.fix: Scale up to about 9 in wide and give the post and arms more wood-grain character so the illustration carries more than the type.

designs.title: Ushuaia
designs.why: An attractive scene that reads well, but it is 30% ink with dense hillside hatching that will fill in to a solid slab. At that coverage plastisol becomes a heavy, stiff patch on the back, and that hand is not acceptable on a $50 shirt.
designs.fix: Knock out 30-40% of the dark hillside and water hatching (open the gaps to at least 0.35 mm) to cut coverage under 20% and keep the print soft and detailed.

designs.title: Belize
designs.why: Two unrelated compositions are stacked: the caye scene, then a floating reef chart with stray soundings and a compass. At 3 m it reads as clutter. Checker-tone patches on the pilings will fill in, and the sounding numerals are tiny.
designs.fix: Drop or greatly simplify the chart and enlarge the caye-and-jetty scene so it becomes one strong image above the caption.
